candidate_policy: Prefer P0 planned rows with source_refs, write_scope, test_commands, acceptance, and done_signal.
Do not assign umbrella rows until a planner splits them.
Every implementation row starts with a failing test or fixture update.
Update progress.json and parity docs in the same slice that changes behavior.

phase-0-parser-adaptive.name: Phase 0 - Parser and adaptive selection foundation

items.name: Parse static HTML into queryable documents
items.contract: Parse HTML into a Document that preserves URL/domain metadata and supports CSS selection.
ready_when: A local HTML fixture can be parsed without network access.
acceptance: Document.CSS returns matching elements and Element exposes tag, text, and attributes.

items.name: Save adaptive fingerprints by domain and identifier
items.contract: Persist enough element identity to relocate the same logical element after markup changes while isolating records by domain.
ready_when: An element has been selected from a parsed document.
acceptance: Saved fingerprints are retrievable by domain and identifier.
The default domain path is deterministic when URL metadata is missing.
done_signal: Store tests pass without shared global state.

items.name: Relocate adaptive elements with deterministic scoring
items.contract: Score candidate elements from a changed document and return the best confident match without fabricating low-confidence matches.
ready_when: A fingerprint exists for the current domain and identifier.
acceptance: Relocation handles ID changes, wrapper insertion, no-match cases, best-candidate selection, and tie order.
done_signal: Relocation tests pass and low-confidence candidates return no match.

phase-1-response-fetcher.name: Phase 1 - Response and static fetcher parity

items.name: Response combines HTTP metadata with parsed document behavior
items.contract: Expose a Scrapling-style response surface that carries URL, status, headers, body bytes, encoding, and selector methods over the parsed document.
ready_when: Response interface design records whether Document is embedded, wrapped, or adapted.
acceptance: A local fixture can build a Response and query it with CSS while preserving HTTP metadata.
done_signal: Response tests prove metadata and selector behavior together.

items.name: Static Fetcher and FetcherSession over net/http
items.contract: Fetch static pages with request option merging, default headers, timeout control, cookies, and local HTTP fixture tests.
acceptance: httptest fixtures prove GET, custom headers, cookies, non-2xx responses, redirect policy, and timeout/error classification.
done_signal: Static fetcher tests pass without live network calls.

items.name: File-backed adaptive store with compatibility migration
items.contract: Persist adaptive fingerprints beyond process memory with explicit schema versioning and deterministic migration tests.
ready_when: The in-memory store contract remains stable after response/fetcher design.
acceptance: A file-backed store can save, reload, isolate domains, and reject incompatible schema versions visibly.
done_signal: File store tests pass with temp directories only.

items.name: BrowserFetcher interface and chromedp/playwright adapter decision
items.contract: Define a Go browser fetcher contract for dynamic pages, page actions, wait conditions, resource blocking, and response extraction before binding to an engine.
ready_when: Static Response and FetcherSession behavior is validated.
not_ready_when: The row tries to implement stealth, proxy rotation, and browser actions in one slice.
acceptance: A fake browser engine fixture proves the public contract before choosing the real engine dependency.
done_signal: Browser fetcher contract tests pass without launching a real browser.

items.name: Spider request, result, scheduler, and session contracts
items.contract: Port Scrapling spider concepts into typed Go request/result/session/scheduler interfaces with deterministic fixture scheduling.
ready_when: FetcherSession is complete and request/response behavior is fixture-backed.
not_ready_when: The row includes robots, cache, checkpoint, sitemap templates, and live crawling in the same slice.
acceptance: A fake fetcher drives deterministic scheduling, callback results, and session reuse.
done_signal: Spider core tests pass using only fake fetchers and local fixtures.

items.name: Robots, cache, checkpoint, and stats as separate crawler slices
items.contract: Add production crawler controls after spider core is proven: robots.txt, cache, checkpoint resume, stats, and polite concurrency.
ready_when: Spider core has a stable request/result/scheduler contract.
not_ready_when: This umbrella has not been split into one row per production control.
acceptance: Planner splits this umbrella into robots, cache, checkpoint, and stats rows before builder work.
done_signal: No builder takes this umbrella directly.

phase-5-cli-tooling.name: Phase 5 - CLI, MCP, and Gormes integration

items.name: CLI extraction workflow parity
items.contract: Map Scrapling CLI extract and shell workflows into a Go command surface only after core fetcher and parser behavior is stable.
ready_when: Response and static fetcher APIs are stable enough for command output fixtures.
acceptance: CLI fixtures prove deterministic extraction output and error messages without live network calls.
done_signal: CLI tests pass from local fixtures.

items.name: Gormes web-search tool adapter
items.contract: Expose goscrapling as a production-friendly Go web search/scraping tool for Gormes without importing Gormes runtime dependencies into the core library.
ready_when: Static fetcher and response objects are validated.
Tool input/output schema is designed separately from library APIs.
acceptance: A fake tool call can fetch a local page, extract selected content, and return structured evidence.
done_signal: Integration tests pass without reaching the network.
